hints.title: Compare chords with each curve
hints.body: The trapezium rule replaces each piece of the curve by its straight chord. A chord above the curve contributes too much area; a chord below it contributes too little.
hints.recap: The error depends on chord position rather than whether the curve rises or falls.
hints.pitfall: Use the shape throughout each strip, not just the slope at one point.
hints.pause: Sketch the original parabola with a chord and classify its approximation.

recall.reminder: The error depends on chord position rather than whether the curve rises or falls.
The second derivative describes how the gradient changes. Use that changing gradient, or an accurate parabola sketch, to determine the bending before comparing its chord with the curve.

hints.title: Derive the transformed shapes
hints.body: Write the second curve using the stated input shift. For the reflection, a point and its image have heights whose average is the height of the mirror line.
hints.recap: A reflection in a horizontal line keeps the horizontal coordinate and reverses vertical displacement from the line.
hints.pitfall: Apply the shift before reflecting the resulting height.
hints.pause: Write the two transformed equations, sketch their bending and classify the remaining approximations.

recall.reminder: A reflection in a horizontal line keeps the horizontal coordinate and reverses vertical displacement from the line.

solution:
The original curve f(x)=−2x2+10 is a downward-opening parabola. Its straight chords lie below the curve, so the trapezium rule underestimates the area.

The translated curve is f(x+1)=−2(x+1)2+10. Moving the parabola left keeps its downward-opening shape, so this is also an underestimate.

Reflecting that curve in y=6 gives y=12−f(x+1)=2(x+1)2+2. This parabola opens upward, so its straight chords lie above the curve and the trapezium rule overestimates the area.

Answer B: underestimate, underestimate, overestimate.
knowledgePattern: Track trapezium-rule bias via concavity under transformations
